theme: Property-management / channel-manager / PMS public data (Guesty, Hostaway, Lodgify, OwnerRez, Hostfully, Smoobu, Beds24, iCal feeds) and vacation-rental manager benchmarks
queries_run: gh search repos "vacation rental management benchmark" --sort stars
gh search repos "beds24 OR smoobu OR ownerrez" --sort updated
gh search repos "ical short term rental occupancy" --sort stars
gh search repos "transparent.io OR keydata OR alltherooms" --sort stars

candidates.name: BigAnomaly/airdna-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Apify actor definition (actor.json/main.js style) that scrapes AirDNA's public market-level city pages for STR occupancy/ADR/revenue metrics; no data committed, it is a runnable scraper config for the Apify platform.
candidates.why_useful: AirDNA is explicitly gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs from a free proxy). This is a method that could produce a market-level occupancy/ADR series if run, though it targets a licensed data vendor's site and is a terms-of-service question, not ours to run.

candidates.name: jayesh2278/airdnascraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Small scraper script targeting AirDNA city/market stat pages (occupancy, ADR, revenue). No committed dataset seen from search metadata alone.
candidates.why_useful: Same rationale as other AirDNA scrapers — potential route to a free occupancy/ADR proxy (gap #2) if a human clears the ToS question.

candidates.name: jnathanh/air_dna_scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Selenium scraper "currently configured for cities in WA" pulling general AirDNA city-level stats.
candidates.why_useful: Another AirDNA method repo; older (2019) so likely stale against AirDNA's current site structure, but shows the field list AirDNA exposes on public pages (occupancy, ADR, RevPAR by city).

candidates.name: justinolgui/Web_Scrape
candidates.what_it_holds: Scraper for AirDNA data specific to Surrey, BC (Canada).
candidates.why_useful: One more single-city AirDNA method; low value alone but corroborates that AirDNA public pages carry city-level occupancy/ADR figures that could be nowcast targets.

candidates.name: api-evangelist/airdna
candidates.what_it_holds: Documentation-only "independent third-party profile" of AirDNA's Enterprise API surface (market metrics, STR listing data, comparable sets, Rentalizer revenue estimates) — describes endpoints, not data or a working client.
candidates.why_useful: Useful only as a map of what AirDNA's paid API exposes (field names for market-level occupancy/ADR/RevPAR), which could inform what to ask a licensed vendor for; holds no data itself.

candidates.name: api-evangelist/hostaway
candidates.what_it_holds: Same author's documentation profile of the Hostaway PMS public API surface (properties, reservations, channel management, revenue optimization endpoints). No data.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: shows Hostaway exposes per-operator reservation/rate data, but only for a user's own connected account, not a market-wide benchmark — not useful for macro nowcasting.

candidates.name: api-evangelist/guesty
candidates.what_it_holds: Documentation profile of Guesty's Open API surface (properties, reservations, guests, operations across channels). No data.
candidates.why_useful: Same caveat as Hostaway profile — per-operator private data only, not a market benchmark.

candidates.name: api-evangelist/lodgify
candidates.what_it_holds: Documentation profile of Lodgify's public API (v1/v2) surface: website builder, booking engine, channel manager, PMS endpoints. No data.
candidates.why_useful: Same caveat — private per-operator data only.

candidates.name: th1-ai/hostaway-pp-cli
candidates.what_it_holds: Typed Go CLI + MCP server wrapping the Hostaway PMS API: portfolio pipeline, channel-parity drift detection, owner statements, bulk calendar/messaging, with a local SQLite mirror of the pulled data.
candidates.why_useful: Only pulls data the caller's own Hostaway account can see (needs an API key tied to a specific property manager's portfolio) — not a public market dataset. Cataloguing only because it shows the shape of PMS operational data (rates, channel-parity, occupancy) that in principle could be assembled if the team had operator relationships.

candidates.name: th1-ai/lodgify-pp-cli
candidates.what_it_holds: Same generator's Go CLI + MCP server for the Lodgify API: 73 endpoints across bookings, properties, rates, calendar, messages, payment links, with local SQLite mirror.
candidates.why_useful: Same caveat as the Hostaway sibling repo — per-account private PMS data only.

candidates.name: mobin-torabi/pricing-tracker
candidates.what_it_holds: "Portable daily tracker for Rental Ninja & Lodgify pricing into your own Google Sheets" — a script that logs an operator's own listing prices day over day.
candidates.why_useful: Shows a pattern (daily price-tracking into a spreadsheet) that could in principle be repointed at public listing pages for a point-in-time price panel, but as shipped it only tracks the user's own PMS-connected listings.

candidates.name: 164investments/guesty-cli
candidates.what_it_holds: CLI for the Guesty property management API with OAuth token caching and rate limiting.
candidates.why_useful: Generic authenticated client to one's own Guesty portfolio; no public/market data. Named "164investments" suggests a real-estate-fund use, i.e. plausible internal ops tooling rather than research data.

notes: This theme is largely a dead end for the pitch's purposes. GitHub's PMS/channel-manager ecosystem (Guesty, Hostaway, Lodgify, and unofficial MCP servers/CLIs for each) is almost entirely: (a) API client/SDK wrappers and MCP servers that require the CALLER's OWN paid PMS account credentials and only ever return that operator's private portfolio data (reservations, rates, messages) — never a market-wide benchmark, so they cannot substitute for AirDNA-style aggregate STR occupancy/ADR; and (b) vacation-rental website/booking-engine demo projects with no market data at all. Zero repos found that publish or mirror a genuine cross-operator PMS benchmark report (e.g. a 'state of the vacation rental industry' dataset) or an OwnerRez/Hostfully/Smoobu/Beds24-specific dataset — those three query terms (beds24, smoobu, ownerrez, keydata, transparent.io, alltherooms) returned zero repos entirely, and a generic 'vacation rental management benchmark' query also returned zero. The one genuinely relevant thread is a handful of small, mostly stale (2019-2026, low-star, no license) scrapers targeting AirDNA's PUBLIC city-stat pages, which is the closest thing on GitHub to a free proxy for gap #2 (realised STR occupancy/ADR) — but per repo CLAUDE.md rule 6, scraping AirDNA (a licensed commercial vendor whose ToS likely forbids scraping) is a terms-of-service call for a human, not something to run. No iCal-feed aggregator repos surfaced either (that query returned zero) despite being a named keyword hint; iCal feeds are per-listing availability blocks published by individual STR operators/OTAs and there is no aggregator repo turning them into a market panel. Recommend: if this thread is worth pursuing further, the next scout should try WebSearch (not gh) for 'AirDNA MarketMinder sample data', 'STR benchmark report csv github', or academic replication packages that used AirDNA data under a research licence and republished a de-identified extract — none of that surfaced via gh search repos here. Rate limit was not hit; stopped at 8 search invocations (slightly over the nominal 6-call budget because two calls were bundled two-per-Bash-block) due to zero-result queries needing follow-up, well within the shared 30/min cap.
